page_title: Segue — broadcast audio playout for macOS

sources.entry: Segue - Broadcast audio playout with crossfade, trim, ramp timers, and pause beds for live radio and podcasts. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/pearcenuk/Segue) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Segue
summary.one_liner: Segue is a free, open-source macOS app for broadcast audio playout, aimed at live radio, podcasts, and events.
use_cases: playing out a podcast or event
generating music licensing reports (APRA, PPL, BMI)
moving a show between Macs as a single JSON file
summary.what_it_does: Segue plays a playlist of audio files in order, advancing automatically and crossfading between tracks at set points. Each track can be trimmed in and out on a waveform, and a ramp timer counts down to a chosen cue point, turning red in the final five seconds. Pauses can be inserted so playback waits for the presenter, and a looping music bed can fade in under a live segment. Every start, finish, skip, and fade is timestamped in a play log that can be exported as CSV, and tracks are scanned and normalised to EBU R128 at -23 dBFS.
notable: Per-track crossfade with linear or equal-power curves, plus waveform trim and ramp timers
Play log exported as CSV for music licensing reports
Playlists export as one JSON file per show, keeping trims, fades and tags
caveats: Not signed or notarized with Apple, so first launch requires right-click → Open
Written with Claude Code by a developer who says they cannot code in Swift; presented as-is
Tracks on unmounted network drives are skipped
